claims.text: The starting material is a bulk CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy with a native coarse-grained microstructure and an unmodified surface.
A thin layer of (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 nanoflakes will be spray-coated onto the CoCrFeNi substrate.
An intermediate adhesion-promoting treatment will be applied between the nanoflake layer and the substrate.
The deposited nanoflakes will form a conformal, shear-responsive, triboactive layer at the sliding interface.
Sliding-induced stress will cause the (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 coating to undergo tribocatalytic reactions.
The proposed tribocatalytic reactions will continuously replenish a low-shear lubricious film.
The lubricious film will minimize direct metal-to-metal contact.
The lubricious film will hinder adhesive wear.
The lubricious film will hinder oxidative wear.
The triboactive layer will dynamically adapt to changes in temperature and load.
The adhesion-enhancing interlayer will prevent coating delamination or degradation during high-temperature, high-pressure operation.
Compared with uncoated CoCrFeNi, the coated material will have significantly lower and more stable coefficients of friction.
The coating may produce a coefficient of friction as low as approximately 0.076 at high temperature.
Compared with uncoated CoCrFeNi, the coating will reduce wear rates throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
The intervention will remain effective from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C at approximately 0.9 GPa contact pressure in ambient air.
Performance may fail under extreme thermal cycling or load spikes if coating adhesion is lost.
Prior evidence supports the efficacy of similar two-dimensional lubricious coatings at elevated temperatures.
Long-term coating adhesion and durability across the full temperature range and under varying loads remain uncertain.
